HIL-010.01.reasoning: No code path of the chain writes an image: the only flash action is HumanBench.flash (tools/hil/bench.py:90), which prints the build command and the instructions and then waits on io.ask('Press Enter ...'); rg finds no esptool, picotool, openocd or UF2 copy outside the emulator bench. But the order of the chain breaks the step on a real board: run_chain.py:391-394 opens the serial port (open_device, run_chain.py:228) BEFORE the flash step. On a blank Pico no CDC port exists (usb-ids.json matches only the running ZPLC image, VID 2E8A PID 000A) and the ESP32-S3 has no ids at all, so the chain ends at 'open' with a PortError and the flash instructions are never printed; and if the board already runs ZPLC and the person flashes at the prompt, the port handle opened earlier is dead once the board re-enumerates, because flash_prompt (run_chain.py:427) and handshake never reopen it (reconnect, hil_steps.py:306, is only called by later steps), so the handshake fails with an OSError. The emulated bench hides this because its ptys keep their path across a flash. Fix: run 'open' after 'flash' (or reopen with the reconnect() loop after the prompt) and do not treat a missing port as an error before the flash step.
